newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off, break support.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off, break support.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks tumbled through support on Friday to end sharply lower, as an overnight fall in U.S. stocks and bonds shook sentiment in the local market and share placements weighed on prices.
The Hang Seng index fell 169.19 points to 11,159.02, breaking support at around 11,200. Turnover was HK$7.35 billion, lifted by a share placement by New World Development.

"I guess we have run up against a whole bunch of things today - with the long bond yield ticking up above seven percent and that large placement by New World," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading HG Asia.
The U.S. long bond fell 23/32 on Thursday to yield 7.04 percent and Dow Industrials fell 64.73 points to 5,647.65.
A sharp upward revision in second-quarter U.S. gross domestic product and a surge in July U.S. home sales revived fears of higher interest rates.
"The market is always going to be sensitive when Wall Street makes moves like it did overnight," said Anthony Edwards, director at BZW Asia.

"There is a a lot of digestion going on with New World and Qingling's placements. What puts people off is the perception that there are a lot of companies waiting to come to the market or to raise cash," he said.
New World placed 75 million shares at HK$37.10 and Silver Grant International sold 80 million Qingling Motors shares at HK$2.975.
New World fell HK$0.50 to HK$37.50, Qingling slipped HK$0.075 to HK$2.975 and Silver Grant rose HK$0.01 to HK$1.87.

Lesko said New World's placement had hurt the rest of the property sector. Cheung Kong ended HK$1.50 lower at HK$54.25, Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$1.25 to HK$75.50 and Henderson Land slid HK$0.75 at HK$60.50.
Hopewell Holdings closed HK$0.225 lower at HK$4.125 after hitting a low at HK$4.075 on rumours of a cash call. Hopewell said it had no immediate plans for a rights issue.

Paladin Ltd resumed trading on Friday after being suspended since August 9, 1994. It closed at HK$0.79, having previously traded at HK$0.65. Five Star Investments has made an HK$0.83 per share offer for the firm.
September Hang Seng futures fell 240 points to 11,095.
